title: The whole book
hookLine: a year to read from the Opening to the edge of the juz' you already know
tomorrow: Seven verses, said seventeen times a day

cards: Pick up a printed Qur'an and open it at the front. In an Arabic copy, the front is on the right, because Arabic reads right to left. The first page is short: seven verses, often framed in gold.
Turn it, and the second surah begins and keeps going for dozens of pages. Year one walked this book from the back, where the surahs are short enough to learn in an afternoon.
Year two opens it at the front and reads forward. Today: the whole book.

teach.b: The word Qur'an means a recitation, something read aloud. It shares a root with iqra', read, the command that tradition says came to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the cave. So the book is named for being heard.
The written copy has another name: mushaf, a bound set of pages, the recitation, bound. Now a fact about the order.

teach.h: NOT THE ORDER IT CAME DOWN
teach.b: The book isn't arranged in the order the verses came down. The verses tradition counts as the first revealed sit near the back, in Surah al-Alaq.
The book opens instead with a short prayer and then the long surah al-Baqarah.
Scholars hold that the order of verses within each surah was set by the Prophet himself; on the order of the surahs, some say the same, and others say it came partly from his companions.
Either way, it's the order Muslims read in today, so this year reads that way.
From al-Fatiha, the Opening, through al-Baqarah and the long Medinan surahs, through Yusuf and Maryam and the Cave, onward, to the edge of the part you already walked, the thirtieth juz'.

In Ramadan some read one juz' a night and close the book on the last nights. Bukhari records that the Prophet told a companion, Abdullah ibn Amr, who wanted to read it constantly, to take a month for each reading.
This year takes it a few verses at a time, slow enough to hear each one.

teach.h: A KHATM: A FULL READING, SEALED
teach.b: Muslims call a full reading a khatm, a sealing. This year is a long, slow khatm.

how: Many Muslims keep a fixed daily time for reading the Qur'an, often after the dawn prayer, and aim to complete a full reading, a khatm, over a month, a Ramadan, or longer.

o: one of the thirty parts read in Ramadan
a full reading of the Qur'an, start to finish
the seal stamped on a printed copy of the Qur'an

games.q: a young companion tells the Prophet he wants to read the whole Qur'an again and again. what does the Prophet tell him, as Bukhari records?
o: take a month for each reading.
games.why: a month. in the report the companion pushes for faster, and is allowed a shorter span, but the advice starts with a pace he can keep.

practice: Choose a daily reading time, a slot that already exists in your day: after the dawn prayer, on the bus, with the first coffee, before you sleep.
Picture yourself there tomorrow, with five quiet minutes, opening the book or this app. If you pray, you can say bismillah as you decide.

wordCard.voice: Khatm. A sealing — the name for a full reading of the Qur'an, which this year will be, a long, slow one. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the written copy of the Qur'an, from a root for pages; the Qur'an itself means the recitation.

carryVoice: Your line: from the opening, onward. A few verses at a time is still the whole book. Year two, day one.
